prompts.title: Recent form: wins, draws and losses
prompts.prompt:
9:16 vertical, 8 seconds, for a transcript line about recent results. The lower quarter stays permanently reserved for yellow burned-in Spanish subtitles over a translucent charcoal scrim; no graphic element crosses into that band.

Common stage: charcoal #101412 field, a faint slate #8ca6bf baseline grid, warm white #edf0e6 typography (condensed grotesque headings, tabular figures for values). The top fifth carries the generic Spanish heading 'FORMA RECIENTE' with the smaller subline 'últimos partidos'. Directly under the chart sit the annotation 'muestra' with the sample counts belonging to each fact and the source string attached to each fact, set small in slate.

Statistical presentation: grouped count bars, three per team — 'victorias', 'empates', 'derrotas' — fed by {{home.wins}}, {{home.draws}} and {{home.losses}} for Olympique Lyonnais in lime #c5ed74, and by {{away.wins}}, {{away.draws}} and {{away.losses}} for Crystal Palace in slate #8ca6bf. One shared vertical scale in 'partidos' grows from a common zero baseline with integer Spanish ticks. Spanish team names sit beneath each group. Sample sizes {{home.n}} and {{away.n}} are printed beside their group; if the two samples are unequal the smaller group gets a dashed bracket labelled 'muestra desigual'. Entry: axis draws left to right in about 0.4 seconds, bars grow from zero in a staggered 0.6 second sequence. Main comparison: the tallest bars of each group pulse once with a slim warm white leader line tagging the value. Emphasis: the home group brightens while the away group sits at reduced opacity, then the emphasis swaps on the second beat. Camera: slow push-in of roughly a tenth of the frame height, no rotation. Transition: hard horizontal wipe along the baseline. Exit: bars retract to zero and the grid fades.

Editorial presentation: pure kinetic typography with rhythmic emphasis, no axes, no sample claims and no invented match events. The Spanish words 'VICTORIA', 'EMPATE' and 'DERROTA' snap in as stacked warm white slabs on the beat of the voice; the home bank shifts to lime, the away bank to slate. A lime block titled 'OLYMPIQUE LYONNAIS' and a slate block titled 'CRYSTAL PALACE' trade the upper and lower halves and drift toward the centre line. Emphasis lands on whichever word the narration stresses, scaled up while the others dim. Camera: locked off with a subtle parallax drift. Transition: the two blocks slide off frame in opposite directions. Exit: a final warm white Spanish caption clears into black.

prompts.title: Goals for and against, both teams
prompts.prompt:
9:16 vertical, 9 seconds, for a transcript line about goals scored and conceded. The lower quarter is reserved for permanent yellow burned-in Spanish subtitles and stays clear of all chart furniture.

Common stage: charcoal #101412, warm white #edf0e6 type, lime #c5ed74 assigned to Olympique Lyonnais, slate #8ca6bf to Crystal Palace. Generic Spanish heading 'GOLES' sits top-left with the subline 'a favor y en contra'. The source string attached to each fact and its sample counts are set small in slate beneath the chart baseline.

Statistical presentation: paired bars, two per team, on one shared vertical scale measured in 'goles' with a common zero baseline and integer Spanish ticks. For Olympique Lyonnais the left bar is 'goles a favor' {{home.gf}} and the right bar 'goles en contra' {{home.ga}}; for Crystal Palace the same pair is {{away.gf}} and {{away.ga}}. Labels are unambiguous Spanish and both teams use the identical unit, so nothing is compared across different measures. Sample context appears as {{home.n}} and {{away.n}} partidos with the attached source. Entry: baseline draws in 0.3 seconds, bars rise from zero in a 0.5 second stagger, value tags fade in behind them. Main comparison: the span between a team's two bars is lightly hatched to show the difference in goles, and a thin warm white rule links the two teams' attacking bars at equal height. Emphasis: the tallest bar in frame pulses lime for a beat, then surrenders emphasis to the other team's attacking bar. Camera: gentle vertical drift upward, keeping the baseline anchored. Transition: the bars dissolve into the pitch illustration of the editorial variant. Exit: value tags drop away and the background darkens.

Editorial presentation: an illustrative football pitch in soft perspective, thin warm white lines on charcoal, centre circle glowing lime. A ball travels a curved path from the home half toward the away goal, then a second path returns along a different arc; these are stylised movements only, never claimed as real match events. The Spanish words 'A FAVOR' and 'EN CONTRA' slide along the respective paths. Small slate shields mark defensive blocks, they carry no numbers and no axes. Emphasis: the ball's contact point flares lime with motion-blur streaks. Camera: slow tilt down the length of the pitch. Transition: a whip pan that follows the ball into the next block. Exit: pitch lines retract toward the centre spot and the frame goes dark.

prompts.title: Clean sheets: counts with their samples
prompts.prompt:
9:16 vertical, 8 seconds, for a transcript line about defensive solidity. The lower quarter is permanently reserved for yellow burned-in Spanish subtitles over a translucent scrim.

Common stage: charcoal #101412 background, warm white #edf0e6 type, lime #c5ed74 for Olympique Lyonnais, slate #8ca6bf for Crystal Palace. A generic Spanish heading 'ARCO EN CERO' sits top-left with the subline 'solidez defensiva'. Beneath the chart a small slate caption carries the source string attached to each fact together with its sample counts.

Statistical presentation: two bars only, one per team, showing clean sheet counts — {{home.clean}} for Olympique Lyonnais and {{away.clean}} for Crystal Palace — on a single shared vertical scale in 'partidos' with a common zero baseline and integer Spanish ticks. Under each bar a thin bracket reports the sample it came from, {{home.n}} and {{away.n}} partidos, so the counts are never read apart from their sample. The caption states plainly that counts are compared as counts and are not converted into rates, shares or any derived figure. Entry: baseline and brackets draw in 0.4 seconds, bars rise from zero in 0.5 seconds, value tags fade in last. Main comparison: the two bars stand side by side at equal width, and a slim warm white hairline spans the shorter bar to show the difference in partidos. Emphasis: the taller bar glows lime for one beat while the other holds reduced opacity, then both return to full strength. Camera: locked off with a slow push-in of about a tenth of frame height. Transition: a hard low-to-high wipe. Exit: bars sink to the baseline and the grid fades to black.

Editorial presentation: defensive energy built around a stylised shield, no axes, no sample claims and no invented match events. The shield assembles in the centre of the frame from warm white facets over charcoal, its inner face tinted lime for Olympique Lyonnais and slate for Crystal Palace as the narration moves between the teams. Spanish words such as 'SÓLIDO', 'ORDEN' and 'ARCO EN CERO' orbit the shield edge and lock into place on the stressed syllables. A faint hexagonal chain, like a back line, snaps into position under the shield to suggest structure and discipline. Emphasis: the shield face flares once when the defensive phrase lands. Camera: slow orbit of a few degrees around the shield. Transition: the shield folds inward into a single lime sliver that wipes the frame. Exit: the sliver retracts to centre and the frame drops to charcoal.

prompts.title: Synthesis: recent output versus recent results
prompts.prompt:
9:16 vertical, 10 seconds, for a closing transcript line that weighs both teams. The lower quarter stays permanently reserved for yellow burned-in Spanish subtitles.

Common stage: charcoal #101412, warm white #edf0e6 type, lime #c5ed74 for Olympique Lyonnais, slate #8ca6bf for Crystal Palace. Generic Spanish heading 'EN RESUMEN' top-left, subline 'datos, no pronósticos'. The source string attached to each fact and its sample counts are set small in slate under each pane.

Statistical presentation: two stacked mini panes that summarise one grounded tension, and they never share a scale. Pane A, labelled 'resultados', is a count comparison in 'partidos' with a common zero baseline: {{home.wins}} for Olympique Lyonnais against {{away.wins}} for Crystal Palace. Pane B, labelled 'goles a favor', is a separate count comparison in 'goles' with its own zero baseline: {{home.gf}} against {{away.gf}}. Sample context {{home.n}} and {{away.n}} partidos appears in both panes with the attached source. Only counts from the supplied sample are shown; the catalog holds no published model estimate, so none is drawn, no derived figure is invented and no forecast is made. Entry: divider line draws, then the two panes fill in sequence, 0.4 seconds each. Main comparison: within each pane the two bars flex to their full height together so the eye reads them at the same moment. Emphasis: the winning margin in each pane is underlined once in warm white, then released. Camera: a single slow push-in covering both panes. Transition: a diagonal wipe that follows the divider. Exit: bars collapse to their baselines and the headings fade.

Editorial presentation: team reveals with narrative emphasis, no axes, no sample claims and no invented match events. The frame is split vertically, lime light rising from the lower half for 'OLYMPIQUE LYONNAIS' and slate light descending from the upper half for 'CRYSTAL PALACE'. Spanish phrases 'RESULTADOS' and 'GOLES A FAVOR' assemble letter by letter along the seam, then detach and drift outward as the narration moves on. Names scale up to fill their half, then recede. Emphasis: a white flare travels the seam whenever the voice names a team. Camera: locked off, with a shallow parallax between the two halves. Transition: the halves fold toward each other into a single vertical light bar. Exit: the bar narrows to a hairline, then the frame goes to charcoal.
